title: CBSP21-NOBORROW-001: a manifest satisfies a PR only if the PR brought it
intent: CBSP21 auto-discovery selected the best-covering manifest with no check on authorship, so a PR could be satisfied by a manifest written for an entirely different change. Close it: ownership means the PR's diff adds or modifies the manifest.
behavior_change: A PR that brings no manifest of its own now FAILS both CBSP21 gates instead of borrowing one. Measured blast radius over the 60 most recent merged PRs: 12 would newly fail (20%), all Dependabot two-file dependency bumps, ZERO human-authored PRs. Legitimate PRs that author their own manifest are unaffected. No change to coverage computation, thresholds, or what CBSP21 checks -- only to which manifest may satisfy a PR.

diff_articulation.what_changed: New owned_candidates() in cbsp21_manifest_discovery.py filters candidates to those whose path appears in the diff. Both gates apply it BEFORE select_manifest and fail with a refuse-to-borrow message when nothing is owned. Kept deliberately OUT of select_manifest: that function ranks, this one filters, and the eighteen existing selection tests exercise ranking with changed-file sets that never include a manifest path -- folding ownership into ranking would have broken all eighteen and buried a policy change inside a scoring function. Added .cbsp21/TEMPLATE-dependency-bump.json for the humans who must now author a manifest per bump; it lives OUTSIDE patches/ because discovery globs patches/*.json with no template exclusion, so a template kept there would itself be a live candidate. Five new tests. Second increment: diagnostic split across both gates, plus five regressions including the non-dependency rmos borrow that proves the defect is repository-wide rather than Dependabot-specific.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: Coverage cannot detect this and the first proposed fix proved it. An ownership rule defined as 'declares every changed file outside .cbsp21/' passes #344 perfectly, because dep-sec-pr281-types-node.json genuinely declares packages/client/package.json and package-lock.json for its own PR. Two dependency bumps really do touch the same two files, so the coverage was never coincidental and no file-set rule is capable of separating owned from borrowed. Had that rule been built, its blast-radius measurement would have read 0 newly-failing PRs and looked like evidence of a safe tighten, when it was evidence the predicate did nothing. The distinguishing fact is authorship, and authorship is visible in the diff the gate already computes.

one test bug of my own, caught and fixed: Path stringifies with backslashes on Windows, so an ownership assertion compared against a forward-slash literal and failed. The predicate was correct; the assertion was not.

SECOND INCREMENT (post-review). Review of the branch found a defect in the fix itself: a PR that OWNS its manifest but under-covers reported 'No applicable patch manifest found' -- false and misleading, since a manifest was found and did belong to the PR. Ownership filtering had made that branch reachable for a new reason without updating its message.

diagnostic split applied to BOTH gates: ownership failure ('declares no CBSP21 manifest of its own') is now distinct from coverage failure ('your manifest declares none of the changed files ... This is a COVERAGE failure, not an ownership failure').

invariant stated mechanically: a manifest already present on the base branch is ineligible unless the current PR modifies it. Because a diff lists a manifest only when the PR adds OR modifies it, 'appears in the diff' expresses that exactly, with no added-vs-modified edge case.

five regressions added: base-branch-ineligibility invariant; the NON-DEPENDENCY rmos borrow (reproduced on main: a diff touching only manufacturing_authority_registry.json borrowed rmos-vcarve-converge-001.json at 100%); five historical manifests covering the same files all losing to one brought manifest; a historical manifest still owned when replaying its ORIGINAL PR's diff; an ordinary non-dependency PR with its own manifest unaffected.
py -3.11 -m pytest scripts/ci/test_cbsp21_manifest_discovery.py -q --no-cov -> 28 passed (18 pre-existing + 5 from increment 1 + 5 new)
acceptance re-run after the second increment: #344 reproduction RED, #350 diff PASSED, dep-sec-pr281-types-node.json untouched, self-test PASSED against the full origin/main..HEAD diff

harness error caught during self-test: `git diff --cached --name-only` lists only the second increment's staged files, omitting the manifest committed in increment 1, so the gate correctly reported an ownership failure. The rule was right; the file list was not.

RULED and deliberately NOT built: dependency identity (change_kind/dependency/from/to). Authorship is the broader discriminator -- it closes the non-dependency borrow too -- and dependency/from/to would be self-asserted unless independently verified against the lockfile diff, which is a separate control (dependency diff verification), not this one.

R1 CLOSURE (CBSP21-NOBORROW-001-R1, test-only): added scripts/ci/test_cbsp21_noborrow_checker.py driving the REAL gate scripts against a synthetic Git base->head. NB-014 (no owned manifest -> provenance diagnostic), NB-015 (owned but under-covers -> coverage diagnostic), NB-020 (own in-diff manifest selected over a fully-covering historical one), plus a coverage-gate lockstep case. 4 passed. No checker code changed.

R1 before/after witness reproduced against MAIN's checker vs this branch's, both directions: dependency (package.json+lockfile) and non-dependency (manufacturing_authority_registry.json). MAIN rc=0 (BORROW / false green) in both cases; this branch rc=1 (FAIL-CLOSED) in both. Confirms the fix is general, not Dependabot-specific.

R1 note (flagged, not fixed here): no CI workflow currently executes scripts/ci/test_cbsp21_* (core_ci runs only test_check_contracts_governance.py; cbsp21_gate.yml runs the gate, not pytest). These tests are durable regression pins; wiring them into CI is a separate CBSP21-invocation increment.

THIRD INCREMENT (post-review #2). All three assessment items were real. I initially recorded the third as a fictional filename because scripts/ci/test_cbsp21_noborrow_checker.py did not exist when I searched -- it was being authored concurrently by a parallel Cursor Agent session on this same branch (1de9e9f8) and had not yet been pushed. CORRECTED: not fiction, work in flight. Absence from my checkout was evidence about my checkout, not about the repository.

CI status re-checked rather than assumed unknown: PR #352 is 36 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipping. The ownership check already ran in CI against CI's own changed-file computation and this PR's own gates went green -- the self-test executing in the real environment.

CONFIRMED HOLLOW GUARANTEE: scripts/ci/test_cbsp21_manifest_discovery.py was run by NO workflow. core_ci.yml:50 names exactly one scripts/ci/ file; there is no root testpaths and no repo-root bare pytest. All 31 tests, including the #344 borrow reproduction, existed without executing. A borrow-fix whose own regression test never runs is the defect this PR exists to remove, recursively. Wired into core_ci.yml as a sibling step.

near-miss diagnostics added: on ownership failure the gate now names the manifests that WOULD have covered the diff but were not brought, ranked by coverage, capped at five. On the #344 shape this prints NINE candidates -- the borrow was a population, not a single coincidence with dep-sec-pr281-types-node.json.

changed-file format equivalence: CI computes `git diff --name-only <merge-base> <head>` (forward slashes, space-joined); _norm handles separators; proven empirically by #352's green CBSP21 gate on the Linux runner.

FOLLOW-UP RECORDED, deliberately not built -- CBSP21-NOBORROW-followup: pin the diff-format equivalence directly. Today it is proven by a passing PR rather than a pinned assertion, so it would break silently if either CI's diff format or the normaliser changed. Belt-and-braces on an already-witnessed property; a clean follow-up, not a hold.

INTEGRATION with 1de9e9f8: that commit independently found the same unwired-tests gap and flagged it as a separate increment; this one performs the wiring. The core_ci step therefore globs scripts/ci/test_cbsp21_*.py rather than naming one file, so BOTH test_cbsp21_manifest_discovery.py and the parallel session's test_cbsp21_noborrow_checker.py execute. Naming a single file would have left the other unrun -- the exact defect being closed.

PARALLEL-SESSION INTEGRATION. A Cursor Agent session pushed 1de9e9f8 to this same branch while this increment was in flight. Rebased onto it, never force-pushed. The manifest conflict was resolved as a UNION of both verification blocks rather than by picking a side.

CI step globs scripts/ci/test_cbsp21_*.py instead of naming one file. Naming test_cbsp21_manifest_discovery.py alone would have left the parallel session's test_cbsp21_noborrow_checker.py unrun -- reintroducing the exact defect this PR closes, inside the fix for it.

Running both files together immediately surfaced an integration failure the glob exists to catch: test_nb014_coverage_gate_lockstep errored with UnicodeDecodeError (cp1252) because its subprocess calls did not pin an encoding and the gates print emoji. Verified PRE-EXISTING by checking out 1de9e9f8 alone -- it fails there too, without any changes from this increment. Would pass on the Linux runner and fail for any Windows developer. Fixed with encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' on both calls.
py -3.11 -m pytest scripts/ci/test_cbsp21_*.py -q --no-cov -> 35 passed (31 + the parallel session's 4)

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: The medium item is the accepted friction: every dependency PR must now carry a human-authored manifest, and Dependabot cannot write one. That is the intended outcome rather than a side effect -- the defect was precisely that dependency PRs passed without declaring themselves, and PR #296 (a supabase bump that also silently reverted zod 4 to 3) is the evidence that the undeclared content matters. Auto-generating a manifest was rejected: it would have to invent intent, behavior_change and risk_level, which are the fields a human reads, so the gate would fabricate the very judgement it exists to record.
